target.title: fix(logbook): bound background refresh concurrency
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where slow Logbook background refreshes could stack a new status, days, and timeline request batch every poll interval, while an older day response could overwrite a newer user selection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Silent refreshes now use one state-owned in-flight slot, and load generations ensure only the current day request can publish results or loading/error state. Foreground loading behavior and gateway-day rollover remain unchanged.

## User Impact

The Logbook view no longer builds up repeated gateway work on slow connections, and switching days keeps the newly selected timeline instead of being replaced by a late older response.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/plugin/logbook-controller.test.ts` on Node 24.18.0: 5 tests passed.
- Regression coverage proves pending poll intervals do not start another three-request batch and that a late older-day load cannot overwrite the current day.
- Scoped `oxfmt --check`: passed.
- `git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check`: passed.
- Structured autoreview: clean, no actionable findings.

## Proof

### 2026-07-13 exact-head controlled Logbook controller proof

- Base commit: `370b5150c25961d6b46c32829b5f44a3a9b60557`.
- Exact PR head: `10e39f96c57147fb5fbad6dc8427a542daf73638`.
- Scope: the committed UI regression tests invoke the production `configureLogbookPolling()` and `loadLogbook()` controller paths. They replace only `GatewayBrowserClient.request()` with deferred responses and drive the production 30-second interval with fake timers.
- Command:

  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/plugin/logbook-controller.test.ts --reporter verbose
  ```

- Transcript:

  ```text
  RUN  v4.1.9
  PASS Logbook controller > does not overlap silent poll refreshes and resumes after settlement
  PASS Logbook controller > does not let an older day load overwrite a newer selection
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests       5 passed (5)
  ```

- Observation: the first silent refresh started exactly three gateway requests. Advancing three additional poll intervals while those requests were pending kept the total at three; after settlement, the next interval started exactly one new three-request batch. In the foreground race, day B completed before the deferred day A response; settling A afterward left the selected day, status, day list, timeline, and loading state owned by B.
- Not tested: a live Gateway, SQLite Logbook storage, browser rendering, network transport, or 30-second wall-clock waiting. The gateway request boundary is controlled and timers are simulated, so this proves controller request concurrency and result ownership. Crabbox was unavailable in this environment; hosted fork CI provides the separate exact-head repository validation.

target.title: fix(google-meet): reject nondecimal transcript cursors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `googlemeet transcript --since` accepted hexadecimal and exponent spellings such as `0x10` and `1e0`, silently converting them to different cursor offsets before gateway delegation. Operators resuming from a documented decimal `nextIndex` could therefore request the wrong transcript slice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript cursor now uses the same strict non-negative integer parser as other Google Meet numeric CLI options. Invalid spellings are rejected at the CLI boundary before `googlemeet.transcript` is invoked, while canonical decimal values including `0` continue to route unchanged.

AI-assisted.

## User Impact

`googlemeet transcript --since` now only accepts canonical decimal cursors. Hex, exponent, and fractional spellings fail fast with the existing `--since must be a non-negative safe integer` message instead of reaching the gateway as a different offset.

## Evidence

### Real registered CLI action proof

Validated on exact pushed head `d634eca76c92e8127e0fcf742c540f196a3d7025`, rebased onto `35fb5ee81ac`.

The proof harness calls the production `registerGoogleMeetCli` Commander action with an injected gateway delegate, matching the real CLI registration path used by the Google Meet plugin.

**Before (upstream/main):**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/cli.transcript-since-proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose

PROOF since=0x10 result={"method":"googlemeet.transcript","payload":{"sessionId":"session-1","sinceIndex":16}}
PROOF since=1e0 result={"method":"googlemeet.transcript","payload":{"sessionId":"session-1","sinceIndex":1}}
PROOF since=0 result={"method":"googlemeet.transcript","payload":{"sessionId":"session-1","sinceIndex":0}}
PROOF since=3 result={"method":"googlemeet.transcript","payload":{"sessionId":"session-1","sinceIndex":3}}
```

**After (this branch):**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/cli.transcript-since-proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose

PROOF since=0x10 result={"error":"--since must be a non-negative safe integer"}
PROOF since=1e0 result={"error":"--since must be a non-negative safe integer"}
PROOF since=0 result={"method":"googlemeet.transcript","payload":{"sessionId":"session-1","sinceIndex":0}}
PROOF since=3 result={"method":"googlemeet.transcript","payload":{"sessionId":"session-1","sinceIndex":3}}
```

This shows the production CLI action previously forwarded `0x10` as `sinceIndex: 16` and `1e0` as `sinceIndex: 1`, and now rejects both before gateway delegation while preserving canonical `0` and `3`.

### Focused regression

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/cli.test.ts -t "transcript cursor|non-decimal transcript|cursor-based transcripts"` — 7 passed
- `git diff --check`

No live Meet session, gateway, or OAuth credentials were required.
